scorecard.rationale: Fourteen people with Parkinson disease completed a brewed-green-tea pilot. Mean Fatigue Severity Scale rose from 28.4 to 32.1, and the same cohort medians rose from 27 to 30.5. No comparator, paired variance or exact fatigue p value is available. Isolated caffeine and a postoperative brewed-tea study favored less fatigue in different comparisons. The traditional leaf-use monograph records perceived relief as an indication. Its clinical assessment cites fortified extracts evaluated on EEG or memory and an acute blend of caffeine and L-theanine with a lower task-tiredness rating. Uncontrolled oncology extract toxicity included fatigue. Whole brewed tea, blended constituents and extracts remain different exposures. The close Parkinson observation retains a tentative worsening direction while the opposite leads remain visible. A controlled Parkinson brew trial and the complete Jiang fly report remain open.
